english.title: Cause to be given away to the public a product / coupon which promotes a tobacco product
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) in the course of a business caused the giving away of a

(A)_[product, namely **(..SPECIFY PRODUCT..),]_
(B)_[coupon]_

to the public, the purpose or effect of which was to promote a tobacco product, namely **(..SPECIFY TOBACCO PRODUCT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 9(1)(b) and 16(2) of the Tobacco Advertising and Promotion Act 2002.
english.pointstoprove:
date andlocation
in the course of a business
caused to be given away a product / coupon
to the public in the United Kingdom
and the purpose / effect of giving the product / coupon away
was to promote a tobacco product

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
